thread:
sam: Observed mismatch between the per-route console token totals and the billing ledger after a stream fallback yesterday. Route shows ~1.2k tokens, ledger only ~300. Repro steps below.
kevin: timeline?
sam: user opens stream -> model A started (provisional tokens emitted). toolcall invoked mid-stream, model A hung and router fell back to model B which re-streamed from prefix. Provisional tokens for A were not refunded when fallback occurred. Billing shows final committed tokens for B only. Console aggregates provisional + committed so it looks like double charge.
olivia: that sounds like the stream_start event is currently treated as final in the console. We need a clear provisional vs committed signal in token telemetry. :thinking:
kevin: proposal: add token_event.kind = "provisional" | "committed" | "refunded" and include an idempotency_id so ledger can reconcile. Example events: 
```
{"stream_id":"s-123","idempotency_id":"i-abc","kind":"provisional","tokens":1200}
{"stream_id":"s-123","idempotency_id":"i-abc","kind":"committed","tokens":300}
{"stream_id":"s-123","idempotency_id":"i-abc","kind":"refunded","tokens":900}
```
kevin: idempotency_id should be generated by router on first attempt and preserved across retries/fallbacks.
maria: UX: dashboard needs a toggle to "include provisional" and a rollout chart that overlays provisional vs committed consumption. Product teams keep getting spooked during canaries because provisional spikes look like real usage.
olivia: telemetry note: tag traces/spans with token_recon_key = idempotency_id and emit a reconciliation event at stream terminal states (committed or refunded). That way we can backfill and auto-refund.
kevin: For quota enforcement, we should only decrement customer quota on "committed" events. Provisional events can be shown as a soft reserve but must not block quota. Otherwise canaries will accidentally exhaust live quota.
maria: edge case: toolcall truncation where the tool server returns 412 and we abort mid-stream — need to emit "refunded" for unconsumed tokens and not leave them hanging in the console.
sam: Also, router policy: when we fallback and rehydrate KV cache or restart generation, attach the same idempotency_id so billing can reconcile. Otherwise we end up with two distinct sessions for one user action.
billing-bot: Created BILL-432 to wire up an automated refund pipeline and reconciliation window logic. We'll attempt auto-refund if reconciliation event arrives within 5m of provisional emission. :white_check_mark:
deploy-bot: deploy/staging finished for feature/token-events (rev 1a2b3). :rocket:
sam: I'll draft a short RFC for token_event.kind + migration plan (backfill strategy, ledger reconciliation, dashboard changes). Need reviewers for API + billing migration.
kevin: happy to review.
olivia: +1
maria: +1
sam: RFC link: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/token-event-kinds
kevin: quick follow-up: we also need to think about streaming caching: if prefix cache is used after fallback, committed tokens may be less than provisional. Make sure the refund semantics support partial refunds (i.e., refunded tokens can be < provisional tokens and are calculated by remaining unconsumed tokens).
maria: agree. also add a small example in the RFC for a toolcall that truncates then fallback. Keeps legal/billing folks happier.
sam: thanks — will post RFC by EOD and tag billing + product.
